brief:
In the historic village of Battir, west of Bethlehem, Dar Abu Hassan—a restored traditional home—offers visitors a living window into Palestinian heritage through its ancient stone archways, the Palestine News Network reported. The guesthouse operates as sunlight filters through the structure's architectural elements, showcasing Palestinian building traditions.

The venture maintains cultural practices amid a tourism downturn affecting the West Bank region. Dar Abu Hassan functions as both a preservation effort and a working guesthouse, keeping traditional Palestinian ways of life accessible to visitors during a period of economic pressure on the tourism sector.
dek: BATTIR/West Bank In the historic village of Battir, west of Bethlehem, sunlight filters through the ancient stone archways of Dar Abu Hassan, a restored traditional home that offers visitors a living window into Palestinian heritage.
title: Battir guesthouse preserves Palestinian heritage through restored stone home
